subsystems.name: Gene delivery vector
subsystems.role: delivers genetic instructions so that selected hippocampal neurons produce light-sensitive proteins.

subsystems.name: Light delivery implant
subsystems.role: shines light onto the targeted neurons deep in the brain.

subsystems.name: Neural recording array
subsystems.role: reads the brain's activity to know when and where to stimulate.

subsystems.name: Closed-loop controller
subsystems.role: decides the timing and pattern of stimulation based on recorded activity.

subsystems.name: Power and packaging
subsystems.role: keeps the implant powered and protected inside the body for years.
parts: implantable battery or wireless power receiver

buildSteps.title: Map the memory circuit
buildSteps.detail: Identify which hippocampal neurons encode a given experience, using recording and tagging in animals.

buildSteps.title: Design the gene payload
buildSteps.detail: Choose an opsin and a promoter that make only the target neurons light-sensitive.

buildSteps.title: Deliver the gene
buildSteps.detail: Inject the viral vector into the hippocampus through stereotaxic surgery.

buildSteps.title: Implant the hardware
buildSteps.detail: Surgically place light guides and recording electrodes into the hippocampus.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the system
buildSteps.detail: Test light intensity and stimulation patterns, and record the neural response.

buildSteps.title: Closed-loop encoding
buildSteps.detail: During learning, detect the relevant neural pattern and stimulate precisely to strengthen it.

buildSteps.title: Validate the effect
buildSteps.detail: Measure whether new information is learned faster or retained longer than without stimulation.

buildSteps.title: Miniaturise for chronic use
buildSteps.detail: Shrink electronics, add wireless power and data, and test long-term stability.

prerequisites.why: works in animals and is in early human trials for vision, but not yet for memory.
delivering genes safely and permanently to deep brain neurons remains difficult.
deep brain stimulators exist, but combining light delivery, high-density recording and years of reliability is not solved.
engram cells are identified in rodents, but human memory encoding is far more complex.
existing arrays lose signal over months as scar tissue forms.

pathway.milestone: rodent studies show that optogenetic stimulation of engram cells can create or recall a memory
pathway.unlocks: proof that specific neurons can be artificially driven to encode information.

pathway.milestone: non-human primate work refines gene delivery and light delivery, while human optogenetic vision trials prove basic safety
pathway.unlocks: a realistic path to testing in people.

pathway.milestone: memory prostheses for patients with hippocampal damage use electrical stimulation first
pathway.unlocks: clinical evidence that boosting encoding is possible, even without optogenetics.

pathway.milestone: a fully implantable optogenetic device for learning acceleration
pathway.unlocks: rapid encoding of new information, initially as a therapy and eventually as an enhancement.
